paper_metadata.title: UniLMv2: Pseudo-Masked Language Models for Unified Language Model Pre-Training
paper_metadata.abstract: We propose to pre-train a unified language model for both autoencoding and partially autoregressive language modeling tasks using a novel training procedure, referred to as a pseudo-masked language model (PMLM). Given an input text with masked tokens, we rely on conventional masks to learn inter-relations between corrupted tokens and context via autoencoding, and pseudo masks to learn intra-relations between masked spans via partially autoregressive modeling. With well-designed position embeddings and self-attention masks, the context encodings are reused to avoid redundant computation. Moreover, conventional masks used for autoencoding provide global masking information, so that all the position embeddings are accessible in partially autoregressive language modeling. In addition, the two tasks pre-train a unified language model as a bidirectional encoder and a sequence-to-sequence decoder, respectively. Our experiments show that the unified language models pre-trained using PMLM achieve new state-of-the-art results on a wide range of natural language understanding and generation tasks across several widely used benchmarks.

extraction_data.innovation: Pseudo-Masked LM (PMLM): jointly pre-trains a bidirectional encoder (via Autoencoding with [M] masks) and a sequence-to-sequence decoder (via Partially Autoregressive modeling with [P] pseudo-masks) in a unified framework; reuses context encodings from the AE pass to avoid redundant computation in the PAR pass; uses well-designed position embeddings and self-attention masks to allow PAR factorization steps to access all position embeddings, improving computational efficiency over separate pre-training.

extraction_data.application: Text generation, natural language understanding, machine translation, question answering

extraction_data.attention_mechanism: Multi-head self-attention with relative position bias

extraction_data.innovation: Pseudo-Masked Language Model (PMLM): jointly learns bidirectional language modeling (via autoencoding) and sequence-to-sequence modeling (via partially autoregressive modeling) in a single forward pass; autoencoding provides global masking information to the partially autoregressive component, while partially autoregressive modeling learns intra-relations between masked spans and long-distance dependencies, preventing local shortcuts and improving computational efficiency compared to separate pre-training objectives.
